"""Headline title casing for article and newsletter titles."""

SMALL_WORDS = frozenset({
    "a", "an", "and", "as", "at", "but", "by", "for", "in", "nor",
    "of", "on", "or", "per", "the", "to", "via",
})

_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION = ".,:;!?"


def title_case(text: str) -> str:
    """Return ``text`` in headline title case.

    ``text`` is split on single spaces into words. Each word is converted on
    its own and the words are joined again with single spaces:

    1. A word with an uppercase letter anywhere after its first character
       (such as "iPhone", "NASA" or "McKinsey") is kept exactly as written.
    2. Otherwise, if the word with any trailing ``.,:;!?`` characters removed
       is, in lowercase, one of ``SMALL_WORDS`` (a, an, and, as, at, but, by,
       for, in, nor, of, on, or, per, the, to, via), the word is written in
       lowercase -- unless it is the first or the last word of ``text``, in
       which case its first character is uppercased.
    3. Every other word has its first character uppercased.
    """
    words = text.split(" ")
    result = []
    for index, word in enumerate(words):
        if index > 0 and word.rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION).lower() in SMALL_WORDS:
            result.append(word.lower())
        else:
            result.append(word.capitalize())
    return " ".join(result)

SMALL_WORDS = frozenset({
    "a", "an", "and", "as", "at", "but", "by", "for", "in", "nor",
    "of", "on", "or", "per", "the", "to", "via",
})

_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION = ".,:;!?"


def title_case(text: str) -> str:
    """Return ``text`` in headline title case.

    ``text`` is split on single spaces into words. Each word is converted on
    its own and the words are joined again with single spaces:

    1. A word with an uppercase letter anywhere after its first character
       (such as "iPhone", "NASA" or "McKinsey") is kept exactly as written.
    2. Otherwise, if the word with any trailing ``.,:;!?`` characters removed
       is, in lowercase, one of ``SMALL_WORDS`` (a, an, and, as, at, but, by,
       for, in, nor, of, on, or, per, the, to, via), the word is written in
       lowercase -- unless it is the first or the last word of ``text``, in
       which case its first character is uppercased.
    3. Every other word has its first character uppercased.
    """
    words = text.split(" ")
    result = []

    # Check if there's a colon and if subtitle starts with a small word
    colon_index = -1
    for i, word in enumerate(words):
        if ':' in word:
            colon_index = i
            break

    subtitle_starts_with_small = False
    first_non_small_after_colon = -1
    if colon_index >= 0 and colon_index + 1 < len(words):
        first_subtitle_word = words[colon_index + 1]
        if first_subtitle_word.rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION).lower() in SMALL_WORDS:
            subtitle_starts_with_small = True
            # Find first non-small word after colon
            for i in range(colon_index + 1, len(words)):
                if words[i].rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION).lower() not in SMALL_WORDS:
                    first_non_small_after_colon = i
                    break

    for index, word in enumerate(words):
        # Rule 1: Preserve mixed-case words (uppercase after first character)
        if len(word) > 1 and any(c.isupper() for c in word[1:]):
            result.append(word)
        # Special subtitle rule: if subtitle starts with small word, only capitalize
        # the first non-small word and the last word
        elif subtitle_starts_with_small and index > colon_index:
            if index == first_non_small_after_colon or index == len(words) - 1:
                result.append(word.capitalize())
            else:
                result.append(word.lower())
        # Rule 2: Small words stay lowercase, except at start or end
        elif (index > 0 and index < len(words) - 1 and
              word.rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION).lower() in SMALL_WORDS):
            result.append(word.lower())
        # Rule 3: Everything else gets first character uppercased
        else:
            result.append(word.capitalize())
    return " ".join(result)

"""Headline title casing for article and newsletter titles."""

SMALL_WORDS = frozenset({
    "a", "an", "and", "as", "at", "but", "by", "for", "in", "nor",
    "of", "on", "or", "per", "the", "to", "via",
})

_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION = ".,:;!?"


def title_case(text: str) -> str:
    """Return ``text`` in headline title case.

    ``text`` is split on single spaces into words. Each word is converted on
    its own and the words are joined again with single spaces:

    1. A word with an uppercase letter anywhere after its first character
       (such as "iPhone", "NASA" or "McKinsey") is kept exactly as written.
    2. Otherwise, if the word with any trailing ``.,:;!?`` characters removed
       is, in lowercase, one of ``SMALL_WORDS`` (a, an, and, as, at, but, by,
       for, in, nor, of, on, or, per, the, to, via), the word is written in
       lowercase -- unless it is the first or the last word of ``text``, in
       which case its first character is uppercased.
    3. Every other word has its first character uppercased.
    """
    words = text.split(" ")
    result = []
    for index, word in enumerate(words):
        if index > 0 and word.rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION).lower() in SMALL_WORDS:
            result.append(word.lower())
        else:
            result.append(word.capitalize())
    return " ".join(result)

"""Headline title casing for article and newsletter titles."""

SMALL_WORDS = frozenset({
    "a", "an", "and", "as", "at", "but", "by", "for", "in", "nor",
    "of", "on", "or", "per", "the", "to", "via",
})

_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION = ".,:;!?"


def title_case(text: str) -> str:
    """Return ``text`` in headline title case.

    ``text`` is split on single spaces into words. Each word is converted on
    its own and the words are joined again with single spaces:

    1. A word with an uppercase letter anywhere after its first character
       (such as "iPhone", "NASA" or "McKinsey") is kept exactly as written.
    2. Otherwise, if the word with any trailing ``.,:;!?`` characters removed
       is, in lowercase, one of ``SMALL_WORDS`` (a, an, and, as, at, but, by,
       for, in, nor, of, on, or, per, the, to, via), the word is written in
       lowercase -- unless it is the first or the last word of ``text``, in
       which case its first character is uppercased.
    3. Every other word has its first character uppercased.
    """
    words = text.split(" ")
    result = []

    # Check if there's a colon and if subtitle starts with a small word
    colon_index = -1
    for i, word in enumerate(words):
        if ':' in word:
            colon_index = i
            break

    subtitle_starts_with_small = False
    first_non_small_after_colon = -1
    if colon_index >= 0 and colon_index + 1 < len(words):
        first_subtitle_word = words[colon_index + 1]
        if first_subtitle_word.rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION).lower() in SMALL_WORDS:
            subtitle_starts_with_small = True
            # Find first non-small word after colon
            for i in range(colon_index + 1, len(words)):
                if words[i].rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION).lower() not in SMALL_WORDS:
                    first_non_small_after_colon = i
                    break

    for index, word in enumerate(words):
        # Rule 1: Preserve mixed-case words (uppercase after first character)
        if len(word) > 1 and any(c.isupper() for c in word[1:]):
            result.append(word)
        # Special subtitle rule: if subtitle starts with small word, only capitalize
        # the first non-small word and the last word
        elif subtitle_starts_with_small and index > colon_index:
            if index == first_non_small_after_colon or index == len(words) - 1:
                result.append(word.capitalize())
            else:
                result.append(word.lower())
        # Rule 2: Small words stay lowercase, except at start or end
        elif (index > 0 and index < len(words) - 1 and
              word.rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION).lower() in SMALL_WORDS):
            result.append(word.lower())
        # Rule 3: Everything else gets first character uppercased
        else:
            result.append(word.capitalize())
    return " ".join(result)
